opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Up to this point in Scripture, something becomes very clear. Jesus is not being spoken of as merely a teacher or prophet, but as the begotten Son—within the Father, through the Father, one with Him. Paul speaks of the disciples as “witnesses before the people,” men carrying forward what they themselves saw and heard. Then the Psalms say, “You are my Son; this day I have begotten you.” And all of it begins connecting.
Then Jesus Himself, while among His disciples, says:
“I will come back again and take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.”
Say what!!
Because these were not later ideas added onto Him. These were His own words, spoken while still in the flesh, walking among them. And by this point in Scripture, we already know who He is—the divine Christ, the Word made flesh, the great I AM.
So when Jesus says, “I will come back,” I do not hear a parable. I hear the truth. I hear a promise.
And maybe what occurs to me most is the simplicity of it. Some of His final words while here among us were essentially: I will return for you myself. I will bring you home.
Right there in Scripture.
It feels almost impossible to miss. And yet it is difficult for us because we live so bound to time—past, present, future, always moving linearly through things. But Christ speaks as though all things are already known to Him. The betrayal was known. The crucifixion was known. The return is known.
Scripture keeps pointing to this reality over and over again: Christ is not trapped inside time the way we are. The Parousia, the coming of Christ, is spoken of as future, yet at times it almost feels as though it is already unfolding while we ourselves are unfolding within it.
And through all of it, His intention remains clear:
 to bring us to Himself.
That is why I write these things here. I try to point toward Him. Because face-to-face, I struggle to say them. But here in words, and I hope these words find you. But more than that, I hope Christ finds you.
Because what greater company could there be than the One who promised He would come back for you Himself?
